rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says human beings alone among animals combine laughter and weeping.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى خص الإنسان بالضحك والبكاء من بين سائر الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported saying assigns laughter without weeping to monkeys and weeping without laughter to camels.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن القرد وحده يضحك ولا يبكي، وإن الإبل وحدها تبكي ولا تضحك.

rows.speaker: يوسف بن الحسين وطاهر المقدسي
rows.claim: Asked whether angels laugh, Tahir al-Maqdisi answered that none beneath the Throne had laughed since Hell was created.
rows.anchor: وقال يوسف بن الحسين: سئل طاهر المقدسي أتضحك الملائكة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God caused the circumstances that bring about death and life.
rows.anchor: أي قضى أسباب الموت والحياة.

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr reads the phrase as God creating death and life, as in 67:2.
rows.anchor: الذي خلق الموت والحياة [الملك:2] قاله ابن بحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God makes the unbeliever dead through unbelief and gives the believer life through faith.
rows.anchor: أمات الكافر بالكفر وأحيا المؤمن بالإيمان قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata explains death as God acting with justice and life as His bestowal of favor.
rows.anchor: قول عطاء: أمات بعدله وأحيا بفضله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes death and life as withholding and miserliness versus generosity and giving.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال: أمات بالمنع والبخل وأحيا بالجود والبذل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God causes the sperm to die and brings the living offspring to life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمات النطفة وأحيا النسمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God causes fathers to die and sons to live.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمات الآباء وأحيا الأبناء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may describe drought and fertility, respectively.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يريد بالحياة الخصب وبالموت الجدب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is sleep followed by waking.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أنام وأيقظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is death in this world and revival for resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمات في الدنيا وأحيا للبعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The male and female pair refers to Adam’s descendants, not Adam and Eve, since neither was created from sperm.
rows.anchor: أي من أولاد آدم ولم يرد آدم وحواء بأنهما خلقا من نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa means a small quantity of water and derives from the verb for water dripping.
rows.anchor: والنطفة الماء القليل، مشتق من نطف الماء إذا قطر.

rows.speaker: الكلبي والضحاك وعطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: They explain tumnā as sperm being poured into the womb.
rows.anchor: تصب في الرحم وتراق قال الكلبي والضحاك وعطاء بن أبي رباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minā is named for the blood sacrifices poured out there.
rows.anchor: وسميت منى بهذا الاسم لما يمنى فيها من الدماء أي يراق.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says tumnā means to determine or allot; the cited verse uses the verb for what the determiner allots.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو عبيدة. يقال: منيت الشيء إذا قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vessel carried by Noah was a ship made of planks.
rows.anchor: أي على سفينة ذات ألواح.

rows.speaker: قتادة والقرظي وابن زيد وابن جبير
rows.claim: They identify dusur as nails fastening the ship’s planks; Ibn Abbas reports the same through al-Walibi.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني المسامير التي دسرت بها السفينة

rows.speaker: الحسن وشهر بن حوشب وعكرمة
rows.claim: They identify dusur as the ship’s prow, which strikes the waves and pushes water aside.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وشهر بن حوشب وعكرمة: هي صدر السفينة

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi reports Ibn Abbas’s view that dusur means the ship’s keel.
rows.anchor: ورواه العوفي عن ابن عباس قال: الدسر كلكل السفينة.

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines a disār as a fiber cord used to bind the planks together.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: الدسار خيط من ليف تشد به ألواح السفينة.

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ says dusur are cords fastening planks, while also recording nails as an alternative meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح: الدسار واحد الدسر وهي خيوط تشد بها ألواح السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also means pushing or boring; Ibn Abbas applies it to amber driven ashore by the sea, and the text gives spear and personal forms.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في العنبر: إنما هو شيء يدسره البحر دسرا أي يدفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under Our eyes can mean in God’s sight, by His command, or under His protection and care.
rows.anchor: بمرأى منا. وقيل: بأمرنا. وقيل: بحفظ منا وكلاءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings are that the ship moved by revelation, by springs issuing from earth, or under angels’ watch.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بوحينا. وقيل: أي بالأعين النابعة من الأرض. وقيل: بأعين أوليائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says any created thing may be attributed to God; the phrase can mean that it proceeds through His protected agents.
rows.anchor: وكل ما خلق الله تعالى يمكن أن يضاف إليه. وقيل: أي تجرى بأوليائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is illustrated by the saying that an eye among God’s eyes became ill and was not visited.
rows.anchor: كما في الخبر: مرض عين من عيوننا فلم تعده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s eye be upon you is a common expression wishing someone divine protection and care.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الناس للمودع: عين الله عليك أي حفظه وكلاءته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the ship a reward for Noah, who endured his people’s abuse; the lam marks purpose.
rows.anchor: جعلنا ذلك ثوابا وجزاء لنوح على صبره على أذى قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, who was disbelieved refers to Noah, whom his people denied.
rows.anchor: أي جحد ف «من» كناية عن نوح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes who as God and the recompense as punishment for their disbelief in Him.
rows.anchor: كناية عن الله والجزاء بمعنى العقاب أي عقابا لكفرهم بالله تعالى.

rows.speaker: يزيد بن رومان وقتادة ومجاهد وحميد
rows.claim: They read the final verb with fatḥa on kāf and fāʾ, making the flood punishment for whoever disbelieved in God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن رومان وقتادة ومجاهد وحميد «جزاء لمن كان كفر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says only ʿŪj ibn ʿUnuq survived the flood because its water reached only his waist.
rows.anchor: وما نجا من الغرق غير عوج بن عنق كان الماء إلى حجزته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says ʿŪj carried Noah needed teak from Syria, so God thanked him and saved him from drowning.
rows.anchor: فحمل عوج تلك الخشبة إليه من الشام فشكر الله له ذلك، ونجاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We left it as a sign may refer to the flood event as a lesson.
rows.anchor: آية } يريد هذه الفعلة عبرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to leaving Noah’s ship as a sign for later people, so they would learn and not deny messengers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد السفينة تركها آية لمن بعد قوم نوح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God preserved the ship at Baqirdā in the Jazira until early Muslims saw it; later ships turned to ash.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أبقاها الله بباقردى من أرض الجزيرة عبرة وآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muddakir is someone who takes warning and fears; it derives from iftaʿala of dhikr, with consonants shifted and assimilated for ease.
rows.anchor: متعظ خائف، وأصله مذتكر مفتعل من الذكر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats indhār and nudhur as verbal nouns meaning warning.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الإنذار والنذر مصدران.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis takes nudhur as the plural of nadhīr, which itself can mean warning, like nakīr means denial.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «نذر» جمع نذير ونذير بمعنى الإنذار كنكير بمعنى الإنكار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran easy to memorize and helps anyone who seeks to memorize it; the question invites a learner to seek that help.
rows.anchor: أي سهلناه للحفظ وأعنا عليه من أراد حفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, yassarnā means preparing the Quran for remembrance, by analogy with saddling a mount or horse.
rows.anchor: ولقد هيأناه للذكر مأخوذ من يسر ناقته للسفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line depicts a horse prepared for war by saddling and bridling it.
rows.anchor: ويسر فرسه للغزو إذا أسرجه وألجمه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean God prepared the Quran for remembrance, like preparing a mount or horse; the accompanying poetry uses mayssiran for a bridled horse.
rows.anchor:
وقمت إليه باللجام ميسرا
هنالك يجزيني الذي كنت أصنع

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says no revealed book besides the Quran can be recited entirely from memory.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: ليس من كتب الله كتاب يقرأ كله ظاهرا إلا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Israelites read the Torah from a written copy except Moses, Aaron, Joshua, and Ezra; they marveled when Ezra rewrote it from memory after it burned.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: ولم يكن هذا لبني إسرائيل، ولم يكونوا يقرؤون التوراة إلا نظرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eased preservation of His Book for this community so remembrance can take root in them until it becomes like an innate trait.
rows.anchor: فيسر الله تعالى على هذه الأمة حفظ كتابه ليذكروا ما فيه أي يفتعلوا الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the question asks whether anyone will recite the Quran.
rows.anchor: فهل من مدكر } قارىء يقرؤه.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق وابن شوذب
rows.claim: They take the question to invite anyone seeking good and knowledge, who will then receive help.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق وابن شوذب: فهل من طالب خير وعلم فيعان عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is repeated in this surah to draw attention and make the message understood.
rows.anchor: وكرر في هذه السورة للتنبيه والإفهام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says each story of past peoples and messengers is itself a reminder, so the question recurs after each account.
rows.anchor: ما عاملتهم به الأمم، وما كان من عقبى أمورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle hal summons listeners’ implanted understanding as evidence against them; the text assigns the lam to calling forth and haʾ to eliciting.
rows.anchor: تستدعي أفهامهم التي ركبت في أجوافهم وجعلها حجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guilty are turned away from truth; saʿr means burning, with madness as an alternative already given in this surah.
rows.anchor: أي في حيدة عن الحق و «سعر» أي احتراق. وقيل: جنون

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة والنبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, after which the verses about being dragged into Hell and all things created by measure were revealed; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: في صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون رسول الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر والنبي
rows.claim: Tawus heard Companions affirm that everything is decreed, then Ibn Umar quoted the Prophet: everything, including incapacity and competence, is by decree.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " كل شيء بقدر حتى العجز والكيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents the report as refuting the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: وهذا إبطال لمذهب القدرية

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: The common reading puts kull in the accusative; Abu al-Sammal reads it nominatively as the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال «كل» بالرفع على الابتداء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative supplies an implicit verb; the Kufans prefer it because inna calls for a verb, which it is more fitting to supply.
rows.anchor: ومن نصب فبإضمار فعل وهو اختيار الكوفيين لأن إن تطلب الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative better conveys universality; deleting the explanatory verb yields “We created every thing by measure,” while khalaqnāhu cannot modify or explain a preceding word.
rows.anchor: والنصب أدل على العموم في المخلوقات لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunni teaching is that God knew each thing’s measure, state, and time before creating it, then creates what His prior knowledge specified.
rows.anchor: الذي عليه أهل السنة أن الله سبحانه قدر الأشياء أي علم مقاديرها وأحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every event proceeds from God’s knowledge, power, and will; people have only acquisition and effort, enabled through His power, guidance, and inspiration.
rows.anchor: فلا يحدث حدث في العالم العلوي والسفلي إلا وهو صادر عن علمه تعالى وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the Qadari claim that human actions belong to us while lifespans belong to someone else; God alone creates.
rows.anchor: لا كما قالت القدرية وغيرهم من أن الأعمال إلينا والآجال بيد غيرنا

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports that a Najran delegation said actions were theirs and lifespans belonged to others; the verses through 54:49 came down, and the Prophet answered their objection about written sins and punishment by saying they would dispute with God on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قدم وفد نجران على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: الأعمال إلينا والآجال بيد غيرنا

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله والنبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls deniers of divine decrees this community’s Magians and says not to visit their sick, attend their dead, or greet them; Ibn Majah transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر والنبي
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas and Jabir says two groups have no share in Islam: the Murjiʾa and the Qadariyya; Ibn Majah transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وجابر قالا: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس والنبي
rows.claim: A report through al-Nahhas from Anas says Qadariyya who claim good and evil are in human hands have no share in the Prophet’s intercession and neither side belongs to the other.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Muslim reports Ibn Umar dissociating himself from the Qadariyya; the author infers he would dissociate only from unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم أن ابن عمر تبرأ منهم ولا يتبرأ إلا من كافر

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar swears that even an Uhud-sized amount of gold spent by one of them would not be accepted until he believed in predestination.
rows.anchor: لو أن لأحدهم مثل أحد ذهبا فأنفقه ما قبل الله منه حتى يؤمن بالقدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this rejection of unbelievers’ spending to 9:54, where disbelief in God and His Messenger prevents their contributions from being accepted.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله تعالى في المنافقين: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة والنبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that belief in predestination removes worry and grief.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun upon it refers to earth, mentioned at the beginning of the surah; Arabic may refer to earth even without explicit prior mention.
rows.anchor: للأرض، وقد جرى ذكرها في أول السورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the angels thought earth’s inhabitants had perished when this verse came down; after 28:88 was revealed they became certain of death.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة هلك أهل الأرض فنزلت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One blessing in creatures’ passing is that death makes all people equal.
rows.anchor: في الموت، ومع الموت تستوي الأقدام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another blessing is that death transfers people to the abode of recompense and reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وجه النعمة أن الموت سبب النقل إلى دار الجزاء والثواب.

rows.speaker: ابن فورك وأبو المعالي
rows.claim: The author endorses scholars who take God’s face to mean His existence and essence, which alone remains when creation perishes.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ارتضاه المحققون من علمائنا: ابن فورك وأبو المعالي وغيرهم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes face as a reference to God Himself.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الوجه عبارة عنه كما قال:

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي
rows.claim: Abu al-Maʿali says most imams understand face as the Creator’s existence; its endurance when creatures perish supports this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وأما الوجه فالمراد به عند معظم أئمتنا وجود الباري تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary refers readers to its discussion of 2:115 and fuller treatment in al-Kitāb al-Asnā.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في «البقرة» القول في هذا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri reports a view that face is an additional, unqualified attribute through which God turns toward those He chooses to honor.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: قال قوم هو صفة زائدة على الذات لا تكيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the sounder view is that face means God’s existence and essence, as in idioms meaning the point or essence of a matter.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن يقال: وجهه وجوده وذاته، يقال: هذا وجه الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations are that what remains is God made manifest by His proofs, or the direction through which people draw near to Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي يبقى الظاهر بأدلته كظهور الإنسان بوجهه. وقيل: وتبقى الجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jalāl means God’s majesty, greatness, and entitlement to attributes of praise; the word derives from jalla, to be great.
rows.anchor: الجلال عظمة الله وكبرياؤه واستحقاقه صفات المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikram means God deserves reverence and should be declared free of what is unbefitting, such as associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: أي هو أهل لأن يكرم عما لا يليق به من الشرك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet urging people to persistently invoke God as Possessor of Majesty and Honor.
rows.anchor: ألظوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The invocation is also attributed to Ibn Masud and is explained as clinging to that formula in supplication.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه من قول ابن مسعود ومعناه: الزموا ذلك في الدعاء.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd explains ilẓāẓ as adhering persistently to something, also meaning insistent supplication.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: الإلظاظ لزوم الشيء والمثابرة عليه

rows.speaker: سعيد المقبري
rows.claim: Saʿid al-Maqburi tells of a man repeatedly invoking God by this name and hearing that his request had been heard.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد المقبري: أن رجلا ألح فجعل يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse introduces two further gardens in addition to the first pair.
rows.anchor: أي وله من دون الجنتين الأوليين جنتان أخريان.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes below them as lower in rank.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ومن دونهما في الدرج.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes below them as lower in merit.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: ومن دونهما في الفضل.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas assigns palms and trees to the first pair, and crops, plants, and spreading vegetation to the second.
rows.anchor: والجنات لمن خاف مقام ربه فيكون في الأوليين النخل والشجر

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests the lower gardens may be for followers of lesser rank, one for houris and another for immortal youths.
rows.anchor: لأتباعه لقصور منزلتهم عن منزلته، إحداهما للحور العين

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj assigns the first pair to the foremost and near ones, with paired fruits and flowing springs, and the second pair to the people of the right.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هي أربع: جنتان منها للسابقين المقربين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the first gardens are gold for those brought near and the second are silver for the people of the right.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إن الأوليين من ذهب للمقربين، والأخريين من ورق لأصحاب اليمين.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس وأبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits Ibn Abbas’s identification of the first pair as for the near ones and the second pair as for the people of the right; Abu Musa reports likewise.
rows.anchor: رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author endorses this ranking: all four gardens are for those who fear God, but the first pair belongs to those foremost in fear and the second to those of lesser state.
rows.anchor: الجنان الأربع لمن خاف مقام ربه إلا أن الخائفين لهم مراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The springs in the first gardens flow, whereas the later pair’s springs gush but do not run like flowing springs.
rows.anchor: أي فوارتان ولكنهما ليستا كالجاريتين لأن النضخ ذون الجري.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pair is said to have every kind of fruit in pairs, while the second names fruit, date palms, and pomegranates without claiming every kind.
rows.anchor: فعم ولم يخص. وفي الأخريين: { فيهما فاكهة ونخل ورمان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pair has couches lined with brocade, ranked above the green cushions and fine woven carpets of the later pair.
rows.anchor: في الأوليين: { متكئين على فرش بطائنها من إستبرق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pair’s houris resemble ruby and coral; the later pair’s beautiful women are not all as beautiful as those gems.
rows.anchor: في صفة الحور: { كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first gardens have abundant branches, while the later pair is described by deep green color alone; further differences may remain unmentioned.
rows.anchor: وقال في الأوليين: { ذواتآ أفنان } وفي الأخريين { مدهامتان }

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reverses the material ranking: the first gardens are gold and silver, while the second are ruby and emerald, which he says are finer.
rows.anchor: الأخريين من ياقوت وزمرد وهما أفضل من الأوليين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim reads dunāhumā as in front of them and nearer to the Throne, thus taking the later pair as nearer.
rows.anchor: ذهب أبو عبد الله الترمذي الحكيم في نوادر الأصول فقال:

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the first gardens as Eden and Bliss, and the later pair as Firdaws and the Garden of Refuge.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الجنتان الأوليان جنة عدن وجنة النعيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain the gardens as green because of abundant water.
rows.anchor: أي خضراوان من الري قاله ابن عباس وغيره.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the gardens are blackened or very dark.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مسودتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahma means black; the verse describes gardens made black by extreme greenness and wetness, since Arabs call green things black.
rows.anchor: أي سوداوان من شدة الخضرة من الري والعرب تقول لكل أخضر أسود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives dark horses and camels as examples of adham, distinguishes a still blacker color as jaww, and explains idhimām as becoming black.
rows.anchor: والدهمة في اللغة السواد يقال: فرس أدهم وبعير أدهم

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s line describes green or dark troops in a woven covering; the commentary identifies al-sannūr as armor-like clothing.
rows.anchor:
وقال لبيد يرثي قتلى هوازن:
وجاؤوا به في هودج ووراءه
كتائب خضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes Iraq’s villages are called Sawād for their greenness, night is called green, and their greenery can mean a people’s multitude.
rows.anchor: وسميت قرى العراق سوادا لكثرة خضرتها. ويقال لليل المظلم: أخضر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people know God sends down water, the author asks why they do not thank Him with sincere worship and why they deny His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: أي فإذا عرفتم بأني أنزلته فلم لا تشكروني بإخلاص العبادة لي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says ujjāj means intensely salty.
rows.anchor: أي ملحا شديد الملوحة قاله ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it means bitter and useless for drinking, farming, or any other use.
rows.anchor: الحسن: مرا قعاعا لا تنتفعون به في شرب ولا زرع ولا غيرهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: why do you not thank the One who did this for you?
rows.anchor: أي فهلا تشكرون الذي صنع ذلك بكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is kindled by striking damp wood.
rows.anchor: أي أخبروني عن النار التي تظهرونها بالقدح من الشجر الرطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tinder trees are markh and ʿafār; a proverb says every tree contains fire and these two abound in it and ignite readily.
rows.anchor: وهي المرخ والعفار ومنه قولهم: في كل شجر نار، واستمجد المرخ والعفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awraytu means to kindle by striking; warā al-zand yarī describes a firestone producing sparks, with another pronunciation in the verb.
rows.anchor: يقال: أوريت النار إذا قدحتها. وورى الزند يرى إذا انقدح منه النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree that produces the fire-making sticks is markh and ʿafār.
rows.anchor: يعني التي تكون منها الزناد وهي المرخ والعفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is the inventor and creator, people should thank Him and not deny His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: أي المخترعون الخالقون أي فإذا عرفتم قدرتي فاشكروني

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says worldly fire is a reminder of the greater fire.
rows.anchor: يعني نار الدنيا موعظة للنار الكبرى قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says fire is a light by which people see through darkness.
rows.anchor: ومجاهد: تبصرة للناس من الظلام.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says human fire is one part in seventy of Hellfire; when Companions said it sufficed, he explained that the other sixty-nine parts are each as hot as it.
rows.anchor: وصح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning believers who keep God’s limits, the passage turns to those who oppose them; this recalls 8:13.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر المؤمنين الواقفين عند حدوده ذكر المحادين المخالفين لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāddah means hostility and opposition to another’s boundaries; its root sense is resistance, related to iron and a gatekeeper.
rows.anchor: والمحادة المعاداة والمخالفة في الحدود وهو مثل قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines muḥāddah as occupying a boundary opposed to another person’s boundary.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المحادة أن تكون في حد يخالف حد صاحبك.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash take kubitū to mean that they were destroyed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والأخفش: أهلكوا.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes it to mean they were humiliated as earlier peoples were humiliated.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: اخزوا كما أخزي الذين من قبلهم.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd explains the verb as being punished.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: عذبوا.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says it means they were cursed.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: لعنوا.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says they were enraged at the Battle of the Trench; another view locates this at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: غيظوا يوم الخندق. وقيل: يوم بدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people intended may be polytheists or hypocrites.
rows.anchor: والمراد المشركون. وقيل: المنافقون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kubitū may mean “will be crushed,” a promise of victory stated in past tense to make it seem near; it is also said to be a Madhhij dialect.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «كبتوا» أي سيكبتون، وهو بشارة من الله تعالى للمؤمنين بالنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs concern earlier people who opposed God and His Messenger, showing what God did to them.
rows.anchor: فيمن حاد الله ورسوله من الذين قبلهم فيما فعلنا بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage promises disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: فيمن حاد الله ورسوله من الذين قبلهم فيما فعلنا بهم. { وللكافرين عذاب مهين }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is accusative either through attachment to humiliating punishment or an implied “remember,” which magnifies the Day.
rows.anchor: نصب ب «عذاب مهين» أو بفعل مضمر تقديره واذكر تعظيما لليوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will resurrect men and women from their graves all at once.
rows.anchor: أي الرجال والنساء يبعثهم من قبورهم في حالة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will tell them what they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي يخبرهم { بما عملوا } في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recorded their deeds in books while they forgot them, so being shown the records makes the proof against them stronger.
rows.anchor: عليهم في صحائف أعمالهم { ونسوه } هم حتى ذكرهم به في صحائفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is fully aware and observing; nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: مطلع وناظر لا يخفى عليه شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no disagreement that those who settled the abode are the Ansar, who established themselves in Medina before the emigrants.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف أن الذين تبوءوا الدار هم الأنصار الذين استوطنوا المدينة قبل المهاجرين إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-īmān is accusative under a verb other than tabawwaʾ, since settlement applies to places; min qablihim attaches to tabawwaʾ and means before the emigrants.
rows.anchor: «والإيمان» نصب بفعل غير تبوأ لأن التبوء إنما يكون في الأماكن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says the Ansar settled Medina and sincerely embraced faith before the Prophet’s migration to them, not that they believed before the emigrants did.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: والذين تبوءوا الدار من قبل المهاجرين واعتقدوا الإيمان وأخلصوه

rows.speaker: أبو علي والزمخشري
rows.claim: One grammatical explanation coordinates faith with an implied command, like “gather your affair and your partners,” meaning summon the partners.
rows.anchor: أي وادعوا شركاءهم ذكره أبو علي والزمخشري وغيرهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses supply omitted places of faith, understand the Ansar as adhering to home and faith, or treat settling faith as metaphor.
rows.anchor: ويجوز حمله على حذف المضاف كأنه قال: تبوءوا الدار ومواضع الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwaʾ means to become established and settled.
rows.anchor: والتبوء: التمكن والاستقرار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects reading this verse as coordinated with the preceding verse about poor emigrants: the earlier verses discuss Banu Nadir and the distinct allocation of their fay.
rows.anchor: ولو تأملوا ذلك وأنصفوا لوجدوه على خلاف ما ذهبوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author treats 59:9 as a new beginning praising the Ansar, who yielded the fay to emigrants without envy; 59:10 also begins a new sentence.
rows.anchor: ابتداء كلام في مدح الأنصار والثناء عليهم فإنهم سلموا ذلك الفيء للمهاجرين

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ismail ibn Ishaq instead coordinates the Ansar and later arrivals with the preceding passage, making emigrants and Ansar partners in the fay.
rows.anchor: وقال إسماعيل ابن إسحاق: إن قوله { والذين تبوءوا الدار }

rows.speaker: مالك بن أوس وعمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: The segment begins a report that Malik ibn Aws heard Umar recite this verse, but gives no further content here.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك بن أوس: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه هذه الآية
